questions.scenario: A remote host must move from INPUT ACCEPT to DROP without interrupting the current administrative session. What sequence is safest?

options.text: Set DROP first, then add allows after reconnecting
Add established traffic and required service allows, verify them, then set DROP
Flush all rules and stop the firewall service
Allow every port, then set DROP

questions.explanation: Install and verify the required allow path before changing the default policy. Stateful established-traffic handling protects existing flows while explicit rules protect intended services. [Netfilter iptables extensions](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/iptables-extensions.8.html).

questions.scenario: An inbound HTTPS request is allowed and the host sends its reply. Which stateful rule commonly permits that return traffic?
questions.explanation: Conntrack classifies reply packets for an established flow, allowing a stateful policy to permit them without opening arbitrary new inbound connections. [Netfilter conntrack](https://docs.kernel.org/networking/nf_conntrack-sysctl.html).

questions.scenario: INPUT policy is ACCEPT, but ss shows a service only on 127.0.0.1:9000. Remote probes are refused. What should be reviewed first?

options.text: Whether to add an allow-all firewall rule
Whether the public DNS TTL is too long
Whether the service is intentionally loopback-only

questions.explanation: The socket binding, not filtering, limits exposure. Confirm the intended architecture before rebinding an internal service. [ss manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ss.8.html).

questions.scenario: A cloud VM listener is healthy, but remote SYN packets never appear in a host capture. Which two upstream controls deserve inspection?
questions.explanation: Security groups and subnet ACLs can filter traffic before it reaches the host. HTTP cookies and certificate identity occur after transport reaches the endpoint. [AWS VPC security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-security-groups.html), [Network ACLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html).

questions.scenario: A broad ACCEPT rule appears before a specific DROP for port 9000. The DROP counter never increases. Why?

options.text: First-match processing accepts the packet before the later rule

questions.explanation: iptables traverses rules in order and a terminating verdict stops further chain traversal. Inspect line order and counters together. [iptables manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/iptables.8.html).

questions.scenario: A filtered TCP probe times out instead of failing immediately. Which verdict is most consistent with that symptom?
questions.explanation: DROP discards without a rejection response and commonly produces a client timeout. REJECT actively returns an error. [iptables extensions](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/iptables-extensions.8.html).

questions.scenario: A team plans to disable password authentication over SSH. What should happen before the current session is closed?

options.text: Expose SSH to all sources temporarily
Validate the configuration and prove a separate key-based session works

questions.explanation: Validate configuration and test a second administrative path before ending the known-good session. This reduces lockout risk while preserving authentication guarantees. [sshd manual](https://man.openbsd.org/sshd.8).

questions.scenario: A password-guessing source is blocked by fail2ban. What limitation should the incident report preserve?

options.text: It proves every SSH credential is strong
Reactive bans supplement but do not replace preventive controls

questions.explanation: Reactive bans respond after observed failures. Strong authentication, limited exposure, logging, and baseline firewall policy remain necessary. [fail2ban manual](https://manpages.debian.org/fail2ban-client).

questions.scenario: Only corporate administrators should reach SSH. Which two controls reduce exposure without weakening application traffic?

options.text: Restrict port 22 to the management CIDR
Disable TLS on the web service

questions.explanation: Source-scoped SSH and stateful return handling limit administrative exposure while preserving intended flows. Opening SSH globally or weakening unrelated TLS expands risk. [iptables manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/iptables.8.html).

questions.scenario: A client times out, but the host has a route, a live listener, and an increasing DROP counter for that port. Where is the failure localized?
questions.explanation: The route and listener exist, while the matching filter counter moves with the failed probe. That directly localizes the observed attempt to host filtering before TLS or HTTP. [iptables manual](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/iptables.8.html).
